prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location, budget, the size/age of your home, and whether you want the highest-efficiency system or the lowest upfront cost. I can help you find top-rated options in your neighborhood, but first here’s how to pick the best company for replacing your AC and what to ask them.

How to pick the best HVAC contractor
- Look for credentials
  - NATE-certified technicians (industry standard).
  - Proper licensing and insurance for your city/county (ask to see license number and insurance certificate).
  - EPA 608 certification (required to handle refrigerant).
- Experience and local reputation
  - Long track record in Atlanta, lots of recent 4–5 star reviews on Google/Angi/BBB.
  - References from neighbors or Nextdoor are valuable.
- Installation quality, not just price
  - They should perform a Manual J load calculation to size the system — not just base it on “rule of thumb.”
  - Ask for Manual S/Manual D if ductwork changes are needed.
  - They should match equipment to house needs (SEER rating, heat pump vs. traditional split).
- Warranties and parts
  - Manufacturer warranty on the unit and a clear labor/installation warranty (1–10 years depending on company).
  - Ask who honors warranty repairs (contractor vs. manufacturer).
- Transparency and documentation
  - Written, itemized quote (equipment, labor, permits, disposal).
  - Permits pulled and inspections arranged.
  - Clear timeline and cleanup plan.
- Energy savings & rebates
  - They should identify federal/local/utility rebates and submit paperwork if applicable.
- Post‑install service
  - Ask about maintenance plans and seasonal tune-ups.

Red flags
- Very lowball quote with pressure to sign immediately.
- No written quote or unwillingness to show licenses/insurance.
- No load calculation or mismatch between equipment capacity and house size.
- Pay-in-full-upfront requests without clear milestones.

Ballpark costs (Atlanta area, approximate)
- Typical full central AC replacement: roughly $4,000–$10,000 for most homes (mid-range equipment). High-efficiency systems or major ductwork work can push $10k–$15k+.
- Get at least 3 written bids so you can compare scope and not just price.

Names and local sourcing
I don’t want to claim a single “best” company. Some nationally known and regionally strong contractors are active in Atlanta (for example Coolray & Mr. Plumber and local One Hour/Neighborly franchises), but the best fit depends on your zip code and needs. Reviews and performance vary by franchise/location.

If you want, I can:
- Pull up the top 3–5 highly rated HVAC companies in your Atlanta ZIP and summarize recent reviews, credentials, and sample quotes (if available).
- Or prepare a short list of questions to ask contractors on the phone so you can quickly compare quotes.

Tell me your zip code, the age/brand of your current system (if known), and whether you prefer highest-efficiency or lowest upfront cost, and I’ll find local options and next steps.
